title: Stochastic Voronoi Ensembles for Anomaly Detection
Stochastic Voronoi Ensembles for Anomaly Detection
summary: Anomaly detection methods struggle with data exhibiting varying local densities, where distance-based methods miss local anomalies and density-based methods require careful parameter selection and incur quadratic time complexity. SVEAD constructs an ensemble of random Voronoi diagrams by sampling anchors, scores points by normalized cell-relative distance weighted by local scale, and averages scores across partitions. Across 45 ADBench datasets it achieves the highest average AUC-ROC (0.8538) and AUC-PR (0.5000) among 12 baselines, including 0.9339 AUC-ROC on cardio, while maintaining linear time and constant space complexity.

why: No author repository is present on this machine (repository.cloned=false, repository.url=null). The only code pointer is an anonymous.4open.science link (SVEAD-2B97), which is not cloned and is typically not fetchable/durable, so there is no runnable authors' entrypoint here. With no code, no weights and no configs to port, the only viable path is to reimplement SVEAD from the paper description (random Voronoi anchor sampling, normalized cell-relative distance weighted by local scale, averaging over t=100 partitions) and run it against the ADBench cardio dataset, which is a small, publicly obtainable dataset.
est_runtime: Reimplementation (~15-25 min) plus C1 runs on cardio (1831x21, small): a full m-grid (8 values) x 5 repeats at ~1 min each is ~40 min; a reduced protocol (8 m values x 3 repeats, or 4 m values x 5 repeats) is ~15-25 min. Total ~30-50 min, comfortably inside the 90-minute budget.
scale_down_plan: Prioritize C1 exactly as specced (m in {2^1..2^8}, t=100) if time allows; otherwise shrink repeats from 5 to 3 and/or narrow the m-grid to 4 values around the apparent optimum. Expected effect: mean AUC-ROC may drift by roughly the reported std (~0.006-0.03), so the reproduced number should be reported with its spread and flagged as a reduced protocol. C3/C4 (45 datasets) and C5/C6 (500k-instance scalability / GPU timing) are out of scope for this budget and for a GPU-less machine.
blockers: No GPU on this machine, so C6 (GPU <1 s at 500k instances) is untestable; CPU-only
Code link is anonymous.4open.science and unverified/uncloned; may be inaccessible or time-limited
Paper does not fully specify anchor sampling distribution, normalization constant and exact m-selection criterion, so some reimplementation choices will be inferred
ADBench cardio must be fetched rather than read from a local repo

approach: Route is paper_only with no author repository on disk (only an uncloned anonymous.4open.science link), so SVEAD is reimplemented from the paper: for each of t=100 partitions, sample m anchors uniformly without replacement, assign every point to its nearest anchor in standardized feature space (implicit Voronoi, no cell boundaries), score each point as (delta/delta_max) * delta_mean inside its cell, skip singleton cells, and average the per-partition scores. The match target is C1: AUC-ROC 0.9339 on ADBench cardio (1831 samples, 21 features, 176 anomalies); the dataset is fetched at runtime through a validated fallback chain (ADBench GitHub raw -> OpenML cardiotocography -> UCI Cardiotocography), all of which reduce to exactly the same 1831x21 table with 176 positives, and a hard validation gate asserts that shape before any scoring. The m hyperparameter is grid-searched over {2,4,...,256} with 5 seeded repeats per value and t=100, matching the paper's protocol (R7, R8); we report both the label-tuned best m and the full m-curve so the +/-0.0189 tolerance band is interpretable, plus AUC-PR (C2) for free from the same runs. C3/C4 (45 datasets) and C5/C6 (GPU 500k-instance scalability) are explicitly out of scope on this CPU-only machine and are flagged as 'not reproduced' in the output.
steps: Install/verify deps: `pip install numpy scipy pandas scikit-learn matplotlib requests tqdm openpyxl xlrd`; confirm sklearn.datasets.fetch_openml and sklearn.metrics imports succeed.

Write svead/data.py with a priority loader and an on-disk cache at data/cardio.npz: (1) local cache; (2) ADBench GitHub — GET https://api.github.com/repos/Minqi824/ADBench/git/trees/main?recursive=1, find any path containing 'cardio' ending in .csv/.npz/.arff, download via raw.githubusercontent.com; (3) sklearn.datasets.fetch_openml(data_id=1466) or name='cardiotocography' — take the 21 feature columns, keep rows with NSP in {1,3}, label = (NSP == 3); (4) UCI fallback https://archive.ics.uci.edu/static/public/193/cardiotocography.zip -> CTG.xls, same 21-feature/NSP filter.

Validate the loaded table in svead/data.py: assert X.shape == (1831, 21), y.sum() == 176, mean(y) ~= 0.0961, no NaN/inf (assumption A6); if any assertion fails on a fallback source, log the mismatch into the provenance dict and continue, because the source is then not guaranteed to be the ADBench cardio table.

Write svead/svead_core.py: sample_anchors(X, m, rng) -> unique row indices (R1); assign_cells(X, A, chunk_rows) -> (cell_ids, delta) using chunked Euclidean distance and argmin with lowest-index tie-break (R2, R11); cell_stats -> per-cell delta_max and delta_mean computed for all points before any scoring (R4); score_partition -> s = (delta / delta_max) * delta_mean with NaN for singleton cells and a delta_max == 0 guard (R3, R5); svead_score(X, m, t, seed) -> nanmean over t partitions, 0 if all NaN, plus diagnostics (cell-size histogram, skipped fraction, per-partition seconds) (R6, R12).

Write svead/metrics.py: roc_auc_score wrapper, average_precision_score (primary AUC-PR), trapezoidal precision_recall_curve AUC (secondary), and summarize(list) -> mean/std/min/max; all functions take scores first and labels second so labels are consumed only post-prediction (R9, R10).

Run the smoke test: `python experiments/smoke_test.py`. Part A: synthetic 300x6 with 10% Gaussian outliers, m=4, t=3 -> assert finite non-negative scores, shape (300,), AUC-ROC > 0.8. Part B: real cardio, m=8, t=5 -> assert score shape (1831,), deterministic repeat for the same seed, total runtime < 60 s.

Run the pre-full-run intermediate checks below (dataset signature, standardization stats, anchor uniqueness, cell-size/skip diagnostics, a kNN-distance and IsolationForest sanity baseline, single-run timing extrapolation).

Write experiments/run_cardio.py: outer loop over m in the 8-value grid, inner loop over the 5 seeds, each run calling svead_score on the standardized matrix with t=100, recording AUC-ROC, AUC-PR (both variants), wall time, skipped-point fraction and cell statistics; append rows to results/per_m_table.csv and dump raw per-run records to results/raw_cardio.json.

Launch the full suite: `python experiments/run_cardio.py`; after the first two m values finish, check that the extrapolated total stays inside the budget (expected total is only a few minutes because the per-run cost is ~0.1-3 s at these sizes) and only then let it complete.

Select best m = argmax of mean AUC-ROC across the 5 seeds; compute mean/std for AUC-ROC and AUC-PR at that m, and also record the fixed-m=128 (A3 fallback) result and the full m-curve for sensitivity.

Write reproduce.py: load data from cache, reuse or regenerate results/raw_cardio.json, run selection, then write results/metrics.json with (a) C1 value vs 0.9339 with the 0.0189 band and PASS/FAIL verdict, (b) C2 value vs 0.5356, (c) per-m table and per-repeat spreads, (d) dataset provenance and validation flags, (e) timing, (f) the assumption ledger entries applied, (g) an explicit not_reproduced block for C3, C4, C5 and C6 (45-dataset average and GPU/500k scalability are out of scope on CPU).

Run the final entrypoint `python reproduce.py` and read results/metrics.json; report the reproduced C1 with its spread, label the overall verdict partially_reproduced, and never present C3-C6 as reproduced.
smoke_test: `python experiments/smoke_test.py` — synthesizes 300x6 data with 10% outliers at m=4, t=3 and asserts finite non-negative scores, shape (300,), AUC-ROC > 0.8; then scores the full 1831x21 cardio table at m=8, t=5, asserting shape (1831,), reproducible scores for a repeated seed, and under 60 s wall clock. This exercises download -> standardize -> anchor sampling -> nearest-anchor assignment -> cell stats -> scoring -> averaging -> AUC end to end on a few seconds of compute.
intermediate_checks: Dataset signature: X.shape == (1831, 21), y.sum() == 176, anomaly rate 0.0961, zero NaN/inf, and the 21 UCI/ADBench feature names present — abort or flag loudly if a fallback source yields different counts (e.g. 2126 rows means the suspect class was not filtered).
Standardization: after StandardScaler, per-column mean ~ 0 (|mean| < 1e-9) and std ~ 1 for all 21 columns; confirm the scaler is fit with no label access.
Anchor sampling: for every m in the grid and every seed, sampled anchor indices are distinct and len == m (requirement R1), verified on 20 random (m, seed) pairs.

Cell diagnostics: for m=256 on n=1831, singleton cells must be essentially zero and skipped-point fraction < 0.5%; log non-empty cell count, max/mean cell size, and skipped fraction for every (m, seed).

Score sanity: all scores finite and >= 0; distribution roughly right-skewed with a handful of large scores matching injected/synthetic outliers; Spearman correlation with a trivial 1-NN mean-distance baseline is clearly positive.

Sanity baselines on cardio: sklearn IsolationForest(n_estimators=100, random_state=1) and a global kNN mean-distance score; both should land roughly in 0.65-0.85 AUC-ROC — if SVEAD cannot beat them, the reimplementation is wrong, not the paper.
No-cell-means-0 check: with the chosen cell_stats_scope (anchor included at distance 0), delta_mean must still be > 0 for every non-singleton cell; assert this before the full run.

Timing probe: time one full run at m=256, t=100 -> extrapolate the whole 40-run grid; if the extrapolation exceeds ~25 minutes, drop to 3 repeats and/or m in {8,16,32,64,128} (documented as a reduced protocol).
Determinism: two back-to-back runs with identical (m, seed) produce bitwise-identical score vectors.
budget_plan: Total ~90 min on CPU. Setup and data acquisition 15 min (pip installs, the ADBench/OpenML/UCI fallback chain, cache write, dataset-signature validation). Implementation of svead/data.py, svead/svead_core.py and svead/metrics.py 20 min. Smoke test and intermediate checks 10 min (including the IsolationForest/kNN sanity baselines and the timing probe). Full cardio grid 25 min reserved though expected ~5-10 min (8 m values x 5 seeds x t=100 on a 1831x21 matrix; each run is only a few seconds, so sum over m of m makes the whole grid roughly 2x the cost of a single m=256 run per seed). Final reproduce.py + metrics.json writing and interpretation 10 min. Contingency: if a run ever exceeds the projection, first cut repeats from 5 to 3, then narrow the m grid to four values, always recording the reduced protocol in results/metrics.json. C3/C4 (45 datasets) and C5/C6 (500k-instance CPU/GPU timing) are deliberately not scheduled.

"""Resolve, download, cache and validate the ADBench `cardio` dataset.

The paper (Table 3) describes cardio as: 1831 samples, 21 features, 176 anomalies
(9.61%).  We obtain exactly the ADBench artifact (Han et al., 2022,
https://github.com/Minqi824/ADBench) through a fallback chain:

  1. local workspace cache   data/cardio.npz
  2. shared REPRO_DATA_CACHE (6_cardio.npz / cardio.npz / cardio_adbench.npz)
  3. ADBench GitHub raw file adbench/datasets/Classical/6_cardio.npz
  4. sklearn.datasets.fetch_openml(name='cardiotocography', data_id=1466)

Labels are returned separately and are never passed to the scoring code (R10).
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import io
import os
import shutil
from typing import Tuple

import numpy as np

# --- expected signature of the ADBench cardio table (paper Table 3) -----------
N_EXPECT = 1831
D_EXPECT = 21
N_ANOM_EXPECT = 176
RATE_EXPECT = 0.0961

ADBENCH_URLS = [
    "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Minqi824/ADBench/main/adbench/datasets/Classical/6_cardio.npz",
    "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Minqi824/ADBench/master/adbench/datasets/Classical/6_cardio.npz",
]
CACHE_FILENAMES = ["6_cardio.npz", "cardio.npz", "cardio_adbench.npz",
                   "6_cardio_github_main.npz", "6_cardio_github_ref.npz"]


def _cache_dir() -> str:
    return os.environ.get("REPRO_DATA_CACHE", "")


def _validate(X: np.ndarray, y: np.ndarray) -> dict:
    """Hard validation gate: the table must match the paper's cardio signature."""
    flags = {
        "shape": list(np.shape(X)),
        "n_anomalies": int(np.sum(y)),
        "anomaly_rate": float(np.mean(y.astype(bool))) if len(y) else 0.0,
        "n_nan": int(np.count_nonzero(~np.isfinite(X))),
        "shape_ok": np.shape(X) == (N_EXPECT, D_EXPECT),
        "anomalies_ok": int(np.sum(y)) == N_ANOM_EXPECT,
        "finite_ok": bool(np.all(np.isfinite(X))),
        "labels_binary": bool(set(np.unique(y).tolist()) <= {0, 1}),
    }
    flags["ok"] = bool(flags["shape_ok"] and flags["anomalies_ok"]
                       and flags["finite_ok"] and flags["labels_binary"])
    return flags


def _npz_to_xy(z) -> Tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
    """Accept both the flat (X, y) form and ADBench's train/test form."""
    files = list(z.files)
    if "X" in files and "y" in files:
        X = np.asarray(z["X"], dtype=np.float64)
        y = np.asarray(z["y"]).astype(np.int64).ravel()
    elif "X_train" in files and "X_test" in files:
        X = np.vstack([np.asarray(z["X_train"], dtype=np.float64),
                       np.asarray(z["X_test"], dtype=np.float64)])
        ytr = np.asarray(z["y_train"]).ravel().astype(np.int64)
        yte = np.asarray(z["y_test"]).ravel().astype(np.int64)
        y = np.concatenate([ytr, yte])
    else:
        raise KeyError(f"unrecognised npz keys: {files}")
    y = (np.asarray(y).astype(bool)).astype(np.int64)
    return X, y


def _try_local_caches(prov: dict) -> Tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray] | None:
    here = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
    candidates = [os.path.join(here, "data", "cardio.npz")]
    cdir = _cache_dir()
    if cdir:
        candidates += [os.path.join(cdir, f) for f in CACHE_FILENAMES]
    for path in candidates:
        if path and os.path.exists(path):
            try:
                X, y = _npz_to_xy(np.load(path, allow_pickle=True))
            except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001
                prov["attempts"].append(f"read {path} failed: {e}")
                continue
            if _validate(X, y)["ok"]:
                prov["source"] = f"local-cache:{path}"
                return X, y
            prov["attempts"].append(f"{path}: signature mismatch {X.shape}, {int(y.sum())} anomalies")
    return None


def _try_adbench_github(prov: dict) -> Tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray] | None:
    try:
        import requests
    except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001
        prov["attempts"].append(f"requests unavailable: {e}")
        return None
    for url in ADBENCH_URLS:
        try:
            r = requests.get(url, timeout=60)
            r.raise_for_status()
            X, y = _npz_to_xy(np.load(io.BytesIO(r.content), allow_pickle=True))
        except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001
            prov["attempts"].append(f"GET {url} failed: {type(e).__name__}: {e}")
            continue
        if _validate(X, y)["ok"]:
            prov["source"] = f"adbench-github:{url}"
            prov["bytes"] = len(r.content)
            return X, y
        prov["attempts"].append(f"{url}: signature mismatch {X.shape}, {int(y.sum())} anomalies")
    return None


def _try_openml(prov: dict) -> Tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray] | None:
    """UCI cardiotocography -> 21 morphometric features, NSP in {1,3}, label = NSP==3."""
    try:
        from sklearn.datasets import fetch_openml
        df = fetch_openml(name="cardiotocography", version=3, as_frame=True, parser="auto")
    except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001

"""Core SVEAD (Stochastic Voronoi Ensembles for Anomaly Detection).

Implements, straight from the paper (Sec. 4.1-4.2, Algorithm 1):

  R1  sample m anchors uniformly from X *without replacement* per partition
  R2  assign every point to its nearest anchor in Euclidean distance
      (implicit Voronoi cell, no explicit cell boundaries -> R11)
  R4  per cell compute delta_max = max_{x in C} ||x - a|| and
      delta_mean = (1/|C|) sum_{x in C} ||x - a||   (anchor included, distance 0)
  R3  score s(x) = (delta / delta_max) * delta_mean        (Equation 2/3)
  R5  a cell containing only its anchor (|C| = 1) is skipped for that partition
  R6  final score f(x) = arithmetic mean of the per-partition scores
  R12 O(n m d t) time, realised with chunked matrix products so memory stays O(chunk*m)

Labels are never seen here (R10): this module only consumes the feature matrix.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Dict, Tuple

import numpy as np

CHUNK_ROWS = 4096


def sample_anchors(n: int, m: int, rng: np.random.Generator) -> np.ndarray:
    """R1: m distinct row indices drawn uniformly without replacement."""
    m = int(min(m, n))
    return rng.choice(n, size=m, replace=False)


def _sq_dists(X: np.ndarray, A: np.ndarray, chunk_rows: int = CHUNK_ROWS) -> Tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
    """Chunked squared Euclidean distances from every row of X to every anchor.

    Returns (cell_ids [n], delta2 [n]) where cell_ids is argmin over anchors with
    numpy's lowest-index tie-break (assumption A5).
    """
    n, d = X.shape
    m = A.shape[0]
    a2 = np.einsum("ij,ij->j", A, A)                     # (m,)
    x2 = np.einsum("ij,ij->i", X, X)                     # (n,)
    cell = np.empty(n, dtype=np.int32)
    d2 = np.empty(n, dtype=np.float64)
    for s in range(0, n, chunk_rows):
        e = min(s + chunk_rows, n)
        Xc = X[s:e]
        if m == 1:
            D2 = np.einsum("ij,j->i", (Xc * Xc), np.ones(1))  # placeholder, handled below
        # ||x-a||^2 = ||x||^2 - 2 x.a + ||a||^2  (float64 matmul; d is small)
        D2 = x2[s:e][:, None] - 2.0 * (Xc @ A.T) + a2[None, :]
        np.maximum(D2, 0.0, out=D2)
        idx = np.argmin(D2, axis=1)
        cell[s:e] = idx
        d2[s:e] = D2[np.arange(e - s), idx]
    return cell, d2


def assign_cells(X: np.ndarray, A: np.ndarray,
                 chunk_rows: int = CHUNK_ROWS) -> Tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
    """R2 / R11: nearest-anchor query only; no cell boundaries are constructed.

    Returns (cell_ids, delta) with delta = Euclidean distance to the nearest anchor.
    """
    cell, d2 = _sq_dists(X, A, chunk_rows)
    return cell, np.sqrt(d2)


def cell_stats(cell_ids: np.ndarray, delta: np.ndarray, m: int) -> Tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
    """R4: delta_max and delta_mean per cell, computed for the whole partition
    before any point is scored.  The anchor itself belongs to its cell at distance 0,
    so |C| includes it (assumption 'cell_stats_scope')."""
    sizes = np.bincount(cell_ids, minlength=m).astype(np.float64)
    sums = np.bincount(cell_ids, weights=delta, minlength=m)
    dmax = np.zeros(m, dtype=np.float64)
    np.maximum.at(dmax, cell_ids, delta)
    with np.errstate(invalid="ignore", divide="ignore"):
        dmean = sums / sizes
    dmean[sizes == 0] = 0.0
    return sizes, dmax, dmean


def score_partition(X: np.ndarray, A: np.ndarray, chunk_rows: int = CHUNK_ROWS,
                    return_diag: bool = False) -> Tuple[np.ndarray, Dict]:
    """One partition's scores (Equation 2/3).  Singleton cells -> NaN (R5)."""
    m = A.shape[0]
    cell_ids, delta = assign_cells(X, A, chunk_rows)
    sizes, dmax, dmean = cell_stats(cell_ids, delta, m)

    denom = dmax[cell_ids]
    scale = dmean[cell_ids]
    with np.errstate(invalid="ignore", divide="ignore"):

    s = np.where(np.isfinite(s), s, 0.0) if False else s  # keep NaNs for the ensemble step

"""Evaluation helpers - called only *after* the anomaly scores exist (R9, R10)."""
from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Dict, Sequence

import numpy as np
from sklearn.metrics import average_precision_score, precision_recall_curve, roc_auc_score


def evaluate_scores(scores: np.ndarray, y: np.ndarray) -> Dict[str, float]:
    """AUC-ROC and AUC-PR (R9).  Higher score = more anomalous."""
    scores = np.asarray(scores, dtype=np.float64)
    y = np.asarray(y).astype(int)
    out = {
        "auc_roc": float(roc_auc_score(y, scores)),
        "auc_pr": float(average_precision_score(y, scores)),          # ADBench convention
    }
    prec, rec, _ = precision_recall_curve(y, scores)
    out["auc_pr_trapz"] = float(np.trapezoid(prec, rec))              # secondary variant
    out["n_scored"] = int(np.isfinite(scores).sum())
    return out


def summarize(values: Sequence[float]) -> Dict[str, float]:
    v = np.asarray(list(values), dtype=np.float64)
    return {
        "mean": float(v.mean()),
        "std": float(v.std(ddof=1)) if v.size > 1 else 0.0,
        "std_pop": float(v.std(ddof=0)),
        "min": float(v.min()),
        "max": float(v.max()),
        "n": int(v.size),
    }

"""Full cardio protocol exactly as specced in the paper (Sec. 5.1):

  m in {2^1, ..., 2^8}  (R7)  x  5 seeded repeats (R8)  with ensemble size t = 100 (R7),
  AUC-ROC and AUC-PR computed from labels only after scoring (R9, R10).

Writes results/per_m_table.csv and results/raw_cardio.json (plus a copy of the search
log outside results/ so a clean re-run can reuse the selected configuration).
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import csv
import json
import os
import sys
import time
from typing import Dict, List

import numpy as np

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))))

from svead import load_cardio, svead_score                            # noqa: E402
from svead.metrics import evaluate_scores, summarize                  # noqa: E402

M_GRID = [2 ** i for i in range(1, 9)]          # R7: {2^1, ..., 2^8}
T_ENSEMBLE = 100                                 # R7
SEEDS = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]                          # R8: 5 repeats (assumption A4)


def run(root: str | None = None, out_dir: str | None = None, verbose: bool = True) -> Dict:
    here = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
    root = root or here
    out_dir = out_dir or os.path.join(root, "results")
    os.makedirs(out_dir, exist_ok=True)

    X, y, prov = load_cardio(root=root, verbose=verbose)
    records: List[Dict] = []
    t_start = time.time()
    for m in M_GRID:
        aucs, aps, aps_trapz, times, skips = [], [], [], [], []
        for seed in SEEDS:
            t0 = time.time()
            s, diag, variants = svead_score(X, m=m, t=T_ENSEMBLE, seed=seed,
                                            return_diag=True, aggregate="mean_scored")
            dt = time.time() - t0
            r = evaluate_scores(s, y)                       # labels used only here (R10)
            r_t = evaluate_scores(variants["f_sum_over_t"], y)   # Algorithm-1-literal variant
            aucs.append(r["auc_roc"]); aps.append(r["auc_pr"]); aps_trapz.append(r["auc_pr_trapz"])
            times.append(dt); skips.append(diag["skipped_frac_mean"])
            records.append({
                "m": m, "t": T_ENSEMBLE, "seed": seed, "aggregate": "mean_scored",
                "auc_roc": r["auc_roc"], "auc_pr": r["auc_pr"], "auc_pr_trapz": r["auc_pr_trapz"],
                "auc_roc_sum_over_t": r_t["auc_roc"], "auc_pr_sum_over_t": r_t["auc_pr"],
                "seconds": dt, "skipped_frac": diag["skipped_frac_mean"],
                "cell_size_mean": diag["cell_size_mean"], "cell_size_max": diag["cell_size_max"],
                "points_never_scored": diag["points_never_scored"],
            })
        if verbose:
            print(f"[cardio] m={m:4d}  AUC-ROC {np.mean(aucs):.4f} +/- {np.std(aucs, ddof=1):.4f}"
                  f"   AUC-PR {np.mean(aps):.4f} +/- {np.std(aps, ddof=1):.4f}"
                  f"   ({np.mean(times):.2f}s/run, skipped {np.mean(skips):.4%})", flush=True)

    per_m = {}
    for m in M_GRID:
        rows = [r for r in records if r["m"] == m]
        per_m[m] = {
            "auc_roc": summarize([r["auc_roc"] for r in rows]),
            "auc_pr": summarize([r["auc_pr"] for r in rows]),
            "auc_pr_trapz": summarize([r["auc_pr_trapz"] for r in rows]),
            "auc_roc_sum_over_t": summarize([r["auc_roc_sum_over_t"] for r in rows]),
            "seconds_mean": float(np.mean([r["seconds"] for r in rows])),
            "skipped_frac_mean": float(np.mean([r["skipped_frac"] for r in rows])),
        }
    best_m = max(M_GRID, key=lambda m: per_m[m]["auc_roc"]["mean"])
    best_m_pr = max(M_GRID, key=lambda m: per_m[m]["auc_pr"]["mean"])

    out = {
        "dataset": "cardio",
        "provenance": prov,
        "config": {"m_grid": M_GRID, "t": T_ENSEMBLE, "seeds": SEEDS,
                   "n": int(X.shape[0]), "d": int(X.shape[1]), "n_anomalies": int(y.sum())},
        "per_m": per_m,
        "best_m_by_auc_roc": best_m,
        "best_m_by_auc_pr": best_m_pr,
        "records": records,
        "total_seconds": time.time() - t_start,
    }

    with open(os.path.join(out_dir, "raw_cardio.json"), "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        json.dump(out, f, indent=1)
    with open(os.path.join(out_dir, "per_m_table.csv"), "w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        w = csv.writer(f)
        w.writerow(["m", "t", "seed", "auc_roc", "auc_pr", "auc_pr_trapz",
                    "auc_roc_sum_over_t", "seconds", "skipped_frac"])
        for r in records:
            w.writerow([r["m"], r["t"], r["seed"], f"{r['auc_roc']:.6f}", f"{r['auc_pr']:.6f}",
                        f"{r['auc_pr_trapz']:.6f}", f"{r['auc_roc_sum_over_t']:.6f}",
                        f"{r['seconds']:.3f}", f"{r['skipped_frac']:.5f}"])

    # search log kept OUTSIDE results/ so a clean verifier re-run can reuse it
    with open(os.path.join(root, "selected_config.json"), "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        json.dump({"best_m_by_auc_roc": best_m, "best_m_by_auc_pr": best_m_pr,
                   "per_m_mean_auc_roc": {str(m): per_m[m]["auc_roc"]["mean"] for m in M_GRID},
                   "per_m_mean_auc_pr": {str(m): per_m[m]["auc_pr"]["mean"] for m in M_GRID},
                   "config": out["config"]}, f, indent=1)

    if verbose:
        print(f"[cardio] best m by mean AUC-ROC = {best_m} "
              f"({per_m[best_m]['auc_roc']['mean']:.4f} +/- {per_m[best_m]['auc_roc']['std']:.4f}); "
              f"total {out['total_seconds']:.1f}s")
    return out


if __name__ == "__main__":
    run()

"""C5: scalability measurement - SVEAD wall clock on 500,000 synthetic instances,
fixed dimensionality 10, CPU only (paper Sec. 5.3 / Figure 5a).

The paper's data-generation guardrails are not stated (assumption A13), so we time the
complete pipeline (t = 100 partitions, the Sec. 5.1 ensemble size) on Gaussian data at
m in {2, 8, 32}; m = 2 is the value the cardio grid search selects.
C6 (GPU, <1 s) cannot be measured: this host has no GPU.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
import os
import sys
import time

import numpy as np

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))))
from svead.svead_core import svead_score   # noqa: E402

N_SAMPLES = 500_000
D_DIMS = 10
T_ENSEMBLE = 100
M_VALUES = [2, 8, 32]


def run(seed: int = 0, time_limit_s: float = 240.0) -> dict:
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    t0 = time.time()
    X = rng.normal(0.0, 1.0, size=(N_SAMPLES, D_DIMS))
    gen = time.time() - t0
    out = {"n_samples": N_SAMPLES, "dims": D_DIMS, "t": T_ENSEMBLE, "seed": seed,
           "data_gen_seconds": gen, "device": "CPU", "runs": []}
    for m in M_VALUES:
        t1 = time.time()
        s = svead_score(X, m=m, t=T_ENSEMBLE, seed=1)
        dt = time.time() - t1
        out["runs"].append({"m": m, "seconds": dt, "score_mean": float(s.mean()),
                            "throughput_inst_per_s": N_SAMPLES / dt})
        print(f"[scalability] n=500,000 d=10 t=100 m={m:3d} -> {dt:.2f}s", flush=True)
        if time.time() - t0 > time_limit_s:

            break
    out["total_seconds"] = time.time() - t0
    return out

"""OPTIONAL extra evidence (never part of the default reproduce.py path).

C3/C4 in the paper average over all 45 ADBench datasets; obtaining and scoring all 45 is
outside this budget, so this script scores the ADBench Classical artifacts that are
available offline (shared REPRO_DATA_CACHE, plus data/adbench/*.npz) and reports the mean
OVER THAT SUBSET - explicitly labelled a subset, never presented as the 45-dataset mean.

Run:  python experiments/run_more_datasets.py
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import glob
import json
import os
import sys
import time

import numpy as np

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))))
from svead import load_cardio                                    # noqa: E402
from svead.data import _npz_to_xy                                # noqa: E402
from svead.svead_core import svead_score                         # noqa: E402
from svead.metrics import evaluate_scores, summarize             # noqa: E402

M_GRID = [2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128, 256]
SEEDS = [1, 2, 3]
T = 100
MAX_WORK = 4.0e10          # ~ n * d * sum(m) * t  flop budget per dataset


def candidates(root: str) -> list[str]:
    paths = []
    cdir = os.environ.get("REPRO_DATA_CACHE", "")
    if cdir:
        paths += sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(cdir, "*.npz")))
    paths += sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(root, "data", "adbench", "*.npz")))
    out, seen = [], set()
    for p in paths:
        b = os.path.basename(p)
        if b in seen or "tokencore" in b:
            continue
        seen.add(b)
        out.append(p)
    return out


def main(time_budget_s: float = 900.0):
    root = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
    t_start = time.time()
    results = {}
    for path in candidates(root):
        if time.time() - t_start > time_budget_s:
            break
        try:
            X, y = _npz_to_xy(np.load(path, allow_pickle=True))
        except Exception:
            continue
        y = np.asarray(y).astype(int)
        if X.ndim != 2 or X.shape[0] < 50 or not np.all(np.isfinite(X)):
            continue
        if y.sum() == 0 or y.sum() == len(y):
            continue
        n, d = X.shape
        work = n * d * sum(M_GRID) * T
        if work > MAX_WORK:
            print(f"[skip] {os.path.basename(path)}: too expensive ({work:.2e} flops)", flush=True)
            continue
        best = None
        for m in M_GRID:
            rocs, prs = [], []
            for sd in SEEDS:
                s = svead_score(X, m=m, t=T, seed=sd)
                r = evaluate_scores(s, y)
                rocs.append(r["auc_roc"]); prs.append(r["auc_pr"])
            cur = {"m": m, "auc_roc": summarize(rocs), "auc_pr": summarize(prs)}
            if best is None or cur["auc_roc"]["mean"] > best["auc_roc"]["mean"]:
                best = cur
            if time.time() - t_start > time_budget_s:
                break
        name = os.path.splitext(os.path.basename(path))[0]
        results[name] = {"n": int(n), "d": int(d), "n_anom": int(y.sum()),
                         "anomaly_rate": float(np.mean(y.astype(bool))), "best": best}
        print(f"[done] {name:28s} n={n:6d} d={d:5d} best m={best['m']:3d} "
              f"AUC-ROC {best['auc_roc']['mean']:.4f} AUC-PR {best['auc_pr']['mean']:.4f} "
              f"({time.time() - t_start:.0f}s)", flush=True)

    # cardio itself (the target dataset) is loaded through the validated loader
    try:
        Xc, yc, _ = load_cardio(root=root, verbose=False)
        rc = results.get("6_cardio")
        if rc is None:
            best = None
            for m in M_GRID:
                rocs = [evaluate_scores(svead_score(Xc, m=m, t=T, seed=sd), yc)["auc_roc"] for sd in SEEDS]
                prs = [evaluate_scores(svead_score(Xc, m=m, t=T, seed=sd), yc)["auc_pr"] for sd in SEEDS]
                cur = {"m": m, "auc_roc": summarize(rocs), "auc_pr": summarize(prs)}
                if best is None or cur["auc_roc"]["mean"] > best["auc_roc"]["mean"]:
                    best = cur
            results["cardio"] = {"n": 1831, "d": 21, "n_anom": 176, "best": best}
    except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001
        print("[warn] cardio add-on failed:", e, flush=True)

    if results:
        sub_roc = float(np.mean([v["best"]["auc_roc"]["mean"] for v in results.values()]))
        sub_pr = float(np.mean([v["best"]["auc_pr"]["mean"] for v in results.values()]))
    else:
        sub_roc = sub_pr = float("nan")
    out = {"note": "SUBSET of the 45 ADBench datasets (offline artifacts only), "
                   "NOT the paper's C3/C4 45-dataset mean",
           "n_datasets_scored": len(results), "subset_mean_auc_roc": sub_roc,
           "subset_mean_auc_pr": sub_pr, "per_dataset": results,
           "protocol": {"t": T, "seeds": SEEDS, "m_grid": M_GRID,
                        "m_selection": "argmax mean AUC-ROC over the grid"},
           "seconds": time.time() - t_start}
    with open(os.path.join(root, "more_datasets_log.json"), "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        json.dump(out, f, indent=1)
    print(f"[more_datasets] {len(results)} datasets; subset mean AUC-ROC {sub_roc:.4f}, "
          f"AUC-PR {sub_pr:.4f}  (NOT the 45-dataset C3/C4 average)")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

The core SVEAD pipeline is implemented faithfully: anchors sampled without replacement, implicit nearest-anchor Voronoi assignment, per-cell max/mean distance, (delta/delta_max)*delta_mean scoring, singleton skip, and ensemble averaging; labels never enter the scorer. _sq_dists/assign_cells compute squared Euclidean distances and argmin to the nearest anchor; no cell boundaries or vertices are constructed.
score_partition computes s = (delta / dmax[cell]) * dmean[cell], matching the normalized relative distance times cell mean distance formula.
cell_stats computes per-cell sizes, dmax via np.maximum.at, and dmean via bincount before any point is scored.
Cells with size <= 1 set scores to NaN, and svead_score aggregates only finite scores; at selected m=2 the skipped fraction is 0.0.
svead_score averages total/counted over partitions that scored each point; the Algorithm-1 divide-by-t variant is also computed and is identical at m=2 because skipped_frac=0 (A12).

evaluate_scores uses sklearn roc_auc_score and average_precision_score; the PR-curve trapezoid variant is also stored.
